findings.title: record_checkout blocks forever when <root>/.checkout is a FIFO, hanging the gate run
findings.evidence: record_checkout only guards against a symlink: `[ ! -L "$root/.checkout" ] && printf '%s\n' "$resolved" > "$root/.checkout"`. Opening a FIFO for writing blocks until a reader appears. Reproduced: I extracted the function from run_all_gates.sh, ran `mkfifo <tmp>/fifo-root/.checkout`, then called `record_checkout <checkout> <tmp>/fifo-root <log>` under `perl -e 'alarm 5'`. It never returned and was killed after 5 s (exit 142), with nothing in the log. The sweep side opens the same file with O_NONBLOCK, and its comment says 'a FIFO planted there must not hang the sweep'.
findings.failure_scenario: Something leaves a FIFO (or another non-regular file that blocks on open) at <root>/.checkout. The next run_all_gates.sh hangs in run_swift_test before `swift test` starts. The spec says a failure to write must not fail or skip the gate. This is very unlikely in practice, hence NIT.
findings.fix: Before writing, also require that the path is absent or a regular file, e.g. `{ [ ! -e "$root/.checkout" ] || [ -f "$root/.checkout" ]; } && [ ! -L "$root/.checkout" ] && printf ... >`. Alternatively, write a temp file in $root and `mv -f` it over .checkout. The rename replaces a symlink or FIFO without following or opening it.
